log.msg: Section 5 finding 1: the brief's own 'revive dropped the OpenRouter provider onto Claude billing' theory is NOT supported by the real ledger (openrouter.jsonl) — the Nemotron h1-page agent stayed on nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra on every turn. The $0->$2.84 cost spike was a separate, already-fixed/reconciled key-sharing billing bug (provider.js's key_diff path billed one agent for another's spend; a -$2.84 correction line is already in the ledger). Net real cost of that incident: $0.

Section 5 finding 2 (real bug, fixed): the library.mjs call that produced that run died (a shell timeout) before it could stop_agent, leaving no landing line, so Heartbeat revived the already-finished agent 9 more times over ~7 hours. Fixed in Servex/ext/openrouter/evals/library.mjs: runOne() now writes a landed_at+outcome line to the run's own task.jsonl the instant its result is known, so task_landed() stops the revive regardless of whether stop_agent is ever reached. Full writeup: harness-findings.md.

Built rung 0 of the framework-literacy ladder as two real AITest pages: /framework/ai/tests/rung0-html-to-view/ (today's brief) and rung0-html-to-view-primer/ (same fixture, a one-screen framework primer inlined in the prompt) — HTML to View-helper translation, checked by a new node-side DOM-tree diff (library.mjs's checksTreeMatch), never a judge's opinion. Proved the checker itself correct with a hand-written correct solution (exact match) and a hand-written wrong one (8 real mismatches) before spending anything on a model.

Section 5 finding 3: Agents.js's 2026-10-01 pool-security gate routes every fresh role:minion spawn through the quick-fix pool and refuses outright (no wait) if none is ready. Confirmed the pool is genuinely stuck right now (take_worktree() itself answers 'No worktree could be made ready'), root-caused in the Servex event log to qf-6 being wedged holding a stopped mastermind-servex-9's uncommitted work, which Pool.js correctly refuses to discard. This blocks every minion on the machine, not just this task. Did not run the suggested salvage (Lifecycle.js --salvage qf-6) myself — that is a judgment call for a human or the module's coordinator, not a quick fix from a different task.

Tried library.mjs's own suggested escape hatch, role: task-mastermind, to route around the stuck pool (added a --role flag, default unchanged at minion) — it hit a second, unrelated bug: a task-mastermind agent's id goes through a stricter 64-char Log.js name check that a minion's own long ids never hit (confirmed: a real successful minion run from 2026-10-01 had an 84-character id). So --role task-mastermind is not actually a safe substitute today; documented honestly, not relied on.

Section 5 finding 4: separately, the shared (machine-wide) OpenRouter weekly spend guard was already over pace ($12.69 of $11.02 allowed) before this task's first OpenRouter request, from other concurrent task-masterminds' spend. This task's own $12 budget is moot while that shared guard is tripped — it is a hard refuse, not a smaller allowance. Validated the rung0 pipeline end-to-end intent on claude-haiku (subscription-billed, outside this guard) instead, hit the task-mastermind naming bug there too. Queuing the actual cheap cross-family OpenRouter runs (DeepSeek v4.1 Flash, GPT-6 Luna, Gemini 3.8 Flash) for the moment the pool is salvaged and/or the guard's pace allowance opens back up (it loosens on its own as the week's elapsed fraction grows).

Built the owner's known-answer analysis tools ahead of the infra blockers clearing, so the moment either the pool or the OpenRouter guard opens up, the exact commands are ready: Servex/ext/openrouter/evals/facts.mjs (naming via the existing class-census rule, per-file comment density, module structure completeness) and known-answer.mjs (turns each fact into a question with a computed right answer, inlines the raw facts into a cheap model's prompt per section 5b's 'fewer requests' rule, scores the model's claim by recall/precision against facts.mjs's own output — code checks the claim, never a judge). Not yet run against a real model (same two blockers). The Gemini-mastermind-vs-Sonnet-minions trial is designed but not built: it needs a live minion spawn too, so it is next once the pool is salvaged.
